answer: Latency-bounded location attestation. Each identity must answer nonces from three independent verifiers within round-trip bounds tied to its claimed region; one operator cannot occupy two distant network locations at once. Each response carries an ember of proof: a signed timestamp from every verifier. The prism splits challenges across regions so relayed answers miss deadlines. This fable of cheap identities fails: the attacker pays a real host, power, and regional IP lease per identity, plus hardware that answers within deadline.
